items.prompt: A photorealistic still from a big-budget historical film set in 1451, natural light, shot on a 35mm lens, meticulous period detail. Porto on the river Douro in northern Portugal: a steep granite town climbing the north bank inside its fourteenth-century walls, the fortress-like Romanesque cathedral with two square towers on the hilltop above, tall narrow stone houses with red tile roofs crowding down to the riverside quay of the Ribeira, flat-bottomed river boats with a single square sail moored along it, and on the far south bank green hills and a few stone wine lodges. Soft overcast morning light, a little mist on the river. Camera on the water about 250 to 300 metres from the shore, at water level, horizon exactly at mid-height. The lower half of the frame is calm open water with soft ripples and long reflections, completely empty in the near water and across the left two-thirds: no boats, no quay, no posts, no rocks, nothing close to the camera. The shore and everything on it sit in the middle distance, small with distance. Nothing later than 1451 anywhere: no cars, street lamps, power lines, tyres, concrete, plastic, glass windows, motorboats, ferries, three-masted ships, modern clothing, tall townhouse facades, Baroque or Gothic spires, bridges across the river. No text, no border, no watermark.

A photorealistic photograph of a real full-size 15th-century Portuguese large caravel (caravela latina grande) under sail, about 25 metres long: THREE masts, every one with a large triangular lateen sail on a long slanted yard, the tallest mainmast forward and two smaller masts behind it, a raised stern deck with a rail, a plain white ensign on a thin pole at the stern, a short bowsprit. Bigger and longer than the two-masted caravel in the reference photo, but the same simple build. Seen exactly side-on, bow pointing right, warm late afternoon light from the right. A working ship of the 15th-century Portuguese Discoveries: weathered linen sails, hemp rigging, dark tarred planking. No gunports, no portholes, no gilded carving, no lanterns, no square sails, not a galleon, not a pirate ship. Not a model: a real ship. She is isolated on a solid, flat, evenly lit chroma-key green background (#00b140) filling everything around her, including below the hull: no sea, no sky, no shadow, no floor, no stand, no cradle. The whole ship from the mastheads to the keel in frame, with a margin all round.
